Subject: APAC rollout — quick ask on dedicated pool sizing and timeline

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving faster than expected on the APAC pilot and Procurement asked me to get an initial ask over to you so we can align on SOW and procurement cadence. Quick context:

- Polaris plans to ship an APAC-facing assistant (LLM-based) for Q4 launch; first internal load tests show a steady-state of ~160 qps inference requests at ~75 tokens average (mostly single-turn). Peak spikes of ~600 qps expected during launch windows.
- Primary model family: 13B mix of open Llama variants + a smaller 7B as fallback. Latency requirement: p95 < 350ms for gen workloads.
- Data residency: logs and traces must remain in region; encryption-at-rest required.

Could you send a recommended GPU footprint for APAC (steady / peak / safety buffer), an ETA for provisioning (lead times for Reserved/Dedicated), and a placeholder SOW we can share with Procurement? I attached a short ML profile export.

Also open to a tri-region plan (US/EU/APAC) if that reduces risk; for now Procurement cares most about APAC timing.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Nguyen

Tom —

Appreciate the details and the ML profile. Short answer up front: we can support the APAC pilot with a dedicated pool; I’ve sketched three scenarios below so Procurement can see cost/lead-time tradeoffs. Before we lock numbers I need two quick clarifications: average tokens per response vs per request (you said 75 tokens average — is that output tokens only?), and expected QPS distribution across peak windows (how long do the 600 qps spikes last?).

Sizing (very rough):
- Steady (sustained 160 qps): ~8 x A5000-equivalent (sustained inference, KV cache active) — supports batching/prefetching.
- Launch peak (600 qps for short bursts): burst buffer of additional 10 nodes (on-demand burst pool) or reserve 6 extra A5000-equivalents if Procurement wants guaranteed capacity.
- Safety buffer (planned redundancy / failover across AZs): +20% on top of steady.

Lead times / procurement: Reserved Dedicated pools we can commit within 6–8 weeks (contract + capacity carve). On-demand burst is immediate but subject to region availability.

I’m looping in Grace from Solutions and Soojin from Capacity Planning to firm up the above and produce a short SOW + timeline. Grace — can your team take point on an SOW draft and initial Sizing Worksheet? Soojin / Jordan — could you validate the A5000-equivalent node counts and whether we should recommend fractional tranching for APAC (start smaller + scale on committed milestones)?

Next steps:
- Confirm tokens (output vs total) and spike duration (Tom)
- Sizing worksheet + draft SOW (Grace)
- Node-level validation & lead time confirmation (Soojin / Jordan)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Forwarding Tom's note + Marcus' initial sizing. I started a draft SOW and attached it (see attachment). Please review and add concrete node-level assumptions.

Key asks for sizing worksheet:
- Confirm performance profile: 13B Llama variant — assume 32k KV cache not required; typical generation length 75 tokens (output). If input tokens add materially, flag.
- Target p95: 350ms — we should size for p95 under steady with 10% headroom.
- Availability SLA wanted by Procurement? (Tom, can you confirm whether they need 99.9% or 99.95%?)

My quick math suggests: steady 160 qps -> ~8 A5000-equivalent nodes; add 6 committed reserve nodes for launch to guarantee headroom; keep a 4-node on-demand burst lane for short spikes. That gives a committed minimum of 14 nodes in APAC with a 4-node burst buffer. But I want Soojin/Jordan to sanity-check the per-node throughput under our production runtime (batching & prefix cache enabled).

Subject: Re: APAC rollout — quick ask on dedicated pool sizing and timeline

Thanks all — validated with Capacity and Runtime teams. Notes below are conservative and assume mixed traffic, real-user randomness, and faster model context windows compared to synthetic tests.

Assumptions we used:
- Model: 13B open family; 75 output tokens + avg 20 input tokens -> ~95 tokens total per request.
- Runtime: continuous batching with KV cache on warm requests; p95 target 350ms for gen workloads.
- Node reference: A5000-equivalent = our benchmark for 13B @ 95 tokens on steady batching.

Recommended footprint (APAC) — finalized:
- Committed dedicated (Reserved): 12 A5000-equivalent nodes. This covers steady 160 qps with ~15% headroom and reaches p95 target under expected request mix.
- Committed launch buffer: +6 reserved nodes (bring to 18) if Procurement requires guaranteed launch headroom.
- Burst pool (on-demand): 4 nodes to absorb very short spikes (up to ~600 qps for <30 minutes) — recommended to be configured as burst-only to avoid long-term cost.
- Cross-AZ redundancy: spread reserved nodes across 3 AZs in the APAC region to meet availability goals.

Timeline and procurement path:
- If Polaris signs for 12-node Reserved pool we can provision within ~6 weeks from contract signature (contract + capacity carve + network setup).
- 18-node reserved (including launch buffer) increases provisioning to ~8 weeks due to extra capacity carve and additional subnet/AZ prep.
- Burst pool is available immediately but is subject to short-term regional capacity constraints — we recommend a hybrid approach (12 reserved + 4 burst) for earliest go-live with cost-conscious commitments.

SOW items to include (Grace's draft should call these out):
- Committed node counts, AZ distribution, fallback lanes to US/EU for surge, data residency and KMS requirements, logging/retention windows, and escalation matrix (point-of-contact for capacity issues).

Tom — if you confirm SLA target (99.9% vs 99.95%) and expected spike duration distribution (typical/launch), I’ll finalize a short Sizing Worksheet with explicit per-node throughput numbers and a recommended procurement timeline.
